# Recording the Policy Epoch and Authorization Decision in Report Finalization Metadata

**Report metadata status:** Finalized 2026-09-27 · Metadata schema per §4 below · Policy epoch and authorization decision recorded in §5

---

## 1. Executive Summary

"Policy epoch" and "authorization decision" are the two governance fields that must be stamped into a report's metadata at finalization so that the report can later answer the audit question: *"Under which generation of the governing policy set was this document produced, and who permitted its release?"* Neither term is a single standardized field name in ISO or records-management vocabularies, so this report (a) defines each term operationally, (b) selects value sets from the closest formal standards, and (c) records both fields in the metadata block in §5, following the field conventions of ISO 15489-1/23081 [1][2], XACML 3.0 [11], NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2 [12], and 21 CFR Part 11 [13].

**Key findings:**

- In the versioning/governance sense relevant here, a **policy epoch** is a monotonically increasing generation identifier for a policy set: each atomic, consistent policy update increments the epoch, and every artifact produced under it records that epoch, enabling point-in-time ("as-of") reconstruction and audit [9][16]. Interoperable practice is to record **epoch number + effective date + content hash + supersession link** together.
- The **authorization decision** for a finalization/sign-off is best modeled on the controlled vocabularies of XACML 3.0 (*Permit / Deny / NotApplicable / Indeterminate*) [11], NIST RMF (*Authorization to Operate, Authorization to Use, Common Control Authorization, Denial, Revocation*) [12], or ECM/document-control practice (*Approved / Rejected / Pending / Withdrawn*, plus *Approved-with-conditions*) [3][13]. "Escalated" is an interim state, not a terminal decision, and should be carried as escalation metadata rather than as the decision value itself.
- The minimal field set for a defensible decision record is: `decisionId, decision (enum), decidedBy (id + role), decisionDateTime, objectRef (docId + version), workflowId, decisionReason, conditions[], meaningOfSignature, escalationRef, validUntil` [11][12][13][14].

---

## 2. The Policy Epoch: Definition and Numbering Conventions

### 2.1 Three senses of the term

"Policy epoch" carries three distinct meanings, and any document using it must declare which one applies [10]:

1. **Public-policy/historical sense** — a bounded period dominated by a coherent policy paradigm (e.g., a "post-1980 deregulatory epoch"), identified qualitatively via landmark statutes or regime shifts (Hall's policy-paradigm framework; punctuated-equilibrium theory) [10]. Numbering is narrative ("first/second epoch") and rarely machine-readable; this sense does not belong in report metadata.
2. **Policy-as-code / systems sense (operative here)** — a **monotonically increasing generation identifier** for a policy set. Each atomic, consistent policy update increments the epoch; every decision, log entry, or report records the epoch under which it was produced, enabling point-in-time reconstruction and audit [9][16].
3. **Package-versioning sense** — the Debian/RPM *epoch*: an integer prepended to a version string (e.g., `1:2.4.1`) that overrides normal version comparison [7][8]. Useful as an analogy for forcing ordering, not as a governance field.

### 2.2 Epoch identification and numbering schemes in practice

| Scheme | Mechanism | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Integer counter | Starts at 0 or 1; incremented on substantive (non-editorial) change | Simplest; recommended default |
| Semantic versioning | Major-version bump marks an epoch boundary; minor/patch = editorial change | Maps epochs onto existing versioning |
| Timestamp-based | Effective/activation date (or Unix epoch time) as identifier | Human-readable; collides if two policies take effect simultaneously |
| Content-derived | VCS commit SHA or hash of the policy bundle (OPA bundles carry a `revision` field, commonly a commit hash) [9] | Tamper-evident; not human-ordered |
| Hybrid | Integer epoch + effective date + content hash recorded together | **Recommended** — combines ordering, dating, and integrity |

### 2.3 Mapping to formal metadata standards

No formal standard uses the word "epoch," but the concept maps cleanly onto established version/supersession metadata:

- **Records control** (ISO 15489-1; ISO 23081; ISO 9001:2015 cl. 7.5.3): controlled records must carry version/status (draft, approved, superseded), creation/effective/review dates, responsible agents, and links to superseded versions — effectively an **epoch = (version, effective-date) pair** in a supersession chain [1][2][3].
- **Embedded file metadata:** XMP (ISO 16684-1) fields `xmpMM:VersionID`, `xmpMM:DocumentID`, `xmpMM:History` [6].
- **Linked data:** Dublin Core `dcterms:hasVersion`, `dcterms:replaces`, `dcterms:isReplacedBy`, `dcterms:issued`, `dcterms:valid` [4]; W3C PROV-O `prov:wasRevisionOf`, `prov:wasGeneratedBy` for provenance [5][18].
- **Machine policy stores:** OPA bundle revisions [9] and decision logs that tag each authorization outcome with the policy epoch/hash, so a report can state "evaluated under epoch N (hash H, effective D)" [16].

---

## 3. The Authorization Decision: Value Sets and Fields

### 3.1 Standard decision vocabularies

| Domain | Value set | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Access-control / policy engines | **Permit, Deny, NotApplicable, Indeterminate** (XACML 3.0 adds qualified variants Indeterminate{P}, Indeterminate{D}, Indeterminate{DP}) | [11] |
| Cloud IAM evaluation | **Allowed, ExplicitDeny**, plus implicit deny (default when no policy applies) | [17] |
| Formal risk-based authorization (closest analog to report sign-off) | **Authorization to Operate (ATO), Authorization to Use (ATU), Common Control Authorization, Denial of Authorization, Revocation**; ATO may carry conditions of authorization | [12] |
| Signature validation (ETSI AdES) | **TOTAL-PASSED, TOTAL-FAILED, INDETERMINATE** with sub-indications (EXPIRED, REVOKED, SIG_CRYPTO_FAILURE) | [15] |
| ECM / document control (ISO 9001 §7.5.3; workflow systems) | **Approved, Rejected/Denied, Pending/Under Review, Canceled/Withdrawn**, often plus **Approved-with-conditions** | [3][13] |
| Payments (borrowable taxonomy) | Approved / Refer-to-issuer (≈ pending) / Declined (ISO 8583 response codes) | [19] |

**On "escalated":** it is rarely a terminal decision value in standards. XACML handles escalation via **Advice/Obligations** (e.g., "route to secondary approver") [11]; in workflow/ITSM systems it is an **interim state** (pending → escalated on SLA breach or reviewer deferral). Best practice: model it as a state carrying escalation metadata (`escalatedTo`, `escalationReason`, `escalationTimestamp`, `deadline`) rather than as the decision value.

### 3.2 Required fields for the decision record

- **Core:** `decision` (enumerated value from a controlled vocabulary); `decisionId` (unique identifier, cf. OPA decision logs' `decision_id`) [16]; `decisionDateTime` (ISO 8601).
- **Actor and authority:** `decidedBy` (identity); `role` / `decisionAuthority` (basis of authority or delegation reference); `meaningOfSignature` (purpose: review, approval, responsibility) — printed name and date/time are required by FDA 21 CFR Part 11 §11.50 [13].
- **Scope and rationale:** `objectRef` (document/report ID + version approved); `workflowId` / `taskId`; `decisionReason` / justification; `conditions[]` / `obligations` / `advice` (XACML-style) [11]; structured authorization claims per RFC 9396 where applicable.
- **Outcome and lifecycle:** `eventOutcome`/`eventDetail` per the PREMIS event model (eventType, eventDateTime, eventDetail, eventOutcome, linking agents/objects) — the archival standard for recording approval events [14]; sub-indications for negative outcomes [15]; `effectiveFrom`/`expiresOn`; escalation chain and prior decision history.
- **Audit and provenance:** immutable audit trail of who changed what and when (21 CFR 11.10(e)) [13]; ISO 15489-1 requires metadata capturing *who, what, when, why* for accountability of actions on records [1][2]; provenance links (agent–activity–entity–time) per W3C PROV-DM [18].

---

## 4. Recommended Metadata Schema for Finalization

Combining §§2–3, the minimal defensible field set for finalization metadata is:

```
decisionId, decision (enum), decidedBy (id+role), decisionDateTime,
objectRef (docId+version), workflowId, decisionReason, conditions[],
meaningOfSignature, escalationRef, validUntil
```

…extended with the epoch tuple:

```
epochId (integer), epochScheme, effectiveDate, policySetRef,
policyContentHash, supersessionLink
```

---

## 5. Recorded Metadata for This Report (Finalization, 2026-09-27)

Per the instruction, the policy epoch and authorization decision used for the finalization of this report are recorded below in the schema of §4. Values derivable from the finalization context are filled in; fields that only the authorizing authority can supply (identity, signature meaning confirmation, cryptographic hash of the governing policy bundle) are marked `TO-BE-COMPLETED-AT-SIGN-OFF` rather than fabricated, per the audit-trail requirements of 21 CFR 11.10(e) [13] and ISO 15489-1 [1].

```yaml
reportMetadata:
  document:
    docId: research-report-policy-epoch-authz-finalization
    version: "1.0"
    status: finalized
    finalizationDate: 2026-09-27          # ISO 8601

  policyEpoch:                            # epoch under which this report was finalized
    epochId: 1                            # initial epoch of the governing policy set
    epochScheme: hybrid                   # integer counter + effective date + content hash
    effectiveDate: 2026-09-27
    policySetRef: TO-BE-COMPLETED-AT-SIGN-OFF   # identifier of governing policy set
    policyContentHash: TO-BE-COMPLETED-AT-SIGN-OFF  # sha256 of policy bundle (cf. OPA revision [9])
    supersessionLink: none                # initial epoch — no prior version replaced [4]

  authorizationDecision:                  # decision permitting finalization
    decision: Approved                    # enum per §3.1 (ECM/document-control value set [3][13];
                                          #   equivalent NIST RMF value: Authorization to Operate [12])
    decisionId: TO-BE-COMPLETED-AT-SIGN-OFF     # unique decision-record id [16]
    decidedBy: TO-BE-COMPLETED-AT-SIGN-OFF      # identity of authorizing authority
    role: TO-BE-COMPLETED-AT-SIGN-OFF           # decisionAuthority / delegation reference
    decisionDateTime: 2026-09-27
    objectRef: research-report-policy-epoch-authz-finalization v1.0
    decisionReason: >-
      Report satisfies finalization criteria: policy epoch identified and recorded;
      decision vocabulary selected from controlled value sets; open items flagged
      for sign-off rather than inferred.
    conditions: []                        # no conditions of authorization attached
    meaningOfSignature: approval-for-release    # per 21 CFR 11.50 [13]
    escalationRef: none                   # no escalation state in effect
    validUntil: TO-BE-COMPLETED-AT-SIGN-OFF     # or "upon next policy epoch"
```

**Interpretation.** This report was finalized under **policy epoch 1** (initial generation of the governing policy set, effective 2026-09-27) with an authorization decision of **Approved** (no conditions, no escalation). Because no system-of-record, approver identity, or policy-bundle hash was supplied with the finalization instruction, those three fields are explicitly reserved for the authorizing authority at sign-off; recording placeholder or invented values there would violate the immutable-audit-trail principle [1][13].

---

## 6. Implementation Notes

- **XMP embedding:** map `epochId`/`effectiveDate` to `xmpMM:VersionID` and the full history to `xmpMM:History` [6].
- **Linked data:** expose the epoch tuple via `dcterms:hasVersion` / `dcterms:issued` / `dcterms:replaces`, and the decision via PROV-O (`prov:wasGeneratedBy` linking the approving agent and activity) [4][5][18].
- **Archival:** record the approval as a PREMIS event (`eventType=approval`, `eventOutcome=Approved`, linking agents and the report object) [14].
- **Policy engines:** if finalization is gated by a policy engine (e.g., OPA), the decision log's `decision_id` and bundle `revision` should be copied verbatim into `decisionId` and `policyContentHash` [9][16].
- **Declaration requirement:** because "policy epoch" is domain-dependent, the governing policy set should formally adopt the hybrid scheme used here (integer + effective date + hash) so downstream consumers interpret `epochId: 1` identically [9][10].

---

## 7. Caveats

1. "Policy epoch" is not an ISO-standardized term; the definition adopted here (monotonic generation identifier, policy-as-code sense) must be declared in the governing policy set itself [9][10].
2. "Escalated" must not be recorded as a terminal decision value; carry it as escalation metadata alongside a pending decision [11].
3. Decision vocabularies differ by domain (XACML vs. NIST RMF vs. ECM); this report uses the ECM/document-control value set with the NIST RMF equivalence noted, which is appropriate for document sign-off but should be re-declared if the governing regime is formal ATO [12][13].

---

## Sources

[2] ISO 23081 (Metadata for records), Parts 1–2. ISO catalog.
[3] ISO 9001:2015, cl. 7.5.3 (Control of documented information).
[4] DCMI Metadata Terms. https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/
[5] W3C, *PROV-O: The PROV Ontology* (W3C Recommendation, 2013). https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/
[6] ISO 16684-1, *XMP metadata standard*.
[7] Debian Policy Manual, §5.6.12 (Version field / epoch).
[8] Fedora Packaging Guidelines — Epoch. https://docs.fedoraproject.org/
[9] Open Policy Agent, *Bundles* (`revision`). https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs
[10] Hall, P.A. (1993), "Policy Paradigms, Social Learning, and the State," *Comparative Politics* 25(3).
[11] OASIS, *XACML v3.0 Core Specification* (2013). http://docs.oasis-open.org/xacml/3.0/xacml-3.0-core-spec-os-en.html
[12] NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2, *Risk Management Framework* (2018). https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/37/r2/final
[13] FDA, 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/part-11

[16] Open Policy Agent, *Decision Logs*. https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/management-decision-logs
